pageAdminOnly: Only the owner or an admin can see the server's security checks.
title: Security basics
summaryNotTested: Checks HTTPS, SSH sign-in, updates, open ports and the server health check.
testingNote: Checking the server. This can take up to 3 minutes.
readOnly: Aquarium only reads these settings. It never changes them; each fix below says what to do on the server.
busy: A check is already running. Try again in a minute.
error: Could not run the checks. Try again.
loadError: Could not load the last result.
helper.missing: Some checks need the server's read-only check helper, which isn't installed yet.
helper.refused: The server's check helper is installed, but the server refused to run it.
helper.busy: The server's check helper was busy. Press Test again in a minute.
helper.timeout: The server's check helper took too long and was stopped.
helper.bad_output: The server's check helper gave an answer Aquarium could not read.
helper.how:
On the server, as root, in the Aquarium folder:
install -m 0755 -o root -g root deploy/hermes-security-check /usr/local/sbin/hermes-security-check
visudo -cf deploy/sudoers.d/hermes-security-check && install -m 0440 -o root -g root deploy/sudoers.d/hermes-security-check /etc/sudoers.d/hermes-security-check
The helper only reads settings and takes no options.
cantCheckFix: Needs the server's check helper (see above).
tls.okMany: Secure connection (HTTPS): {count} web addresses, first certificate runs out on {date}
tls.invalid: {domain}: the security certificate is not valid
tls.unreachable: {domain}: no secure connection answers on this server
tls.soon: {domain}: the security certificate runs out in {days} days ({date})
tls.noDomain: Secure connection (HTTPS): no web address is set up yet
tls.noDomainFix: Set up a web address (step 5) so people reach Aquarium over HTTPS.
tls.fix: Fix: make sure the name points at this server and ports 80 and 443 are open. Certificates renew by themselves once that works.
tls.how: On the server: journalctl -u caddy -n 100 shows why the certificate could not be fetched or renewed. Check the name's "A record" at your domain provider points at this server.
ssh.ok: SSH sign-in uses keys only (no passwords)
ssh.password: The server still accepts SSH passwords
ssh.root: SSH lets root sign in with a password
ssh.unreadable: SSH sign-in: the server's SSH settings could not be read
ssh.fix: Fix: add your SSH key to the server, then turn password sign-in off.
ssh.keys: {count} SSH key(s) are already set up on this server.
ssh.noKeys: No SSH key is set up yet. Add one first, or you will lock yourself out.
ssh.how:
1. On your computer: ssh-copy-id root@<your server> (or add your public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server).
2. Open a NEW terminal and check you can sign in with the key. Keep the old one open.
3. On the server, create /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-aquarium.conf with these lines:
   PasswordAuthentication no
   KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
   PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
4. Run: sshd -t && systemctl reload ssh
5. Sign in again from a new terminal before you close the old one.
updates.fix: Fix: turn on Ubuntu's automatic security updates.
updates.how:
On the server: apt-get install unattended-upgrades
then: dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades (choose Yes)
and: systemctl enable --now apt-daily-upgrade.timer
ports.ok: Only SSH (22) and the web (80, 443) are open to the internet
ports.extra: Other ports are open to the internet: {ports}
ports.unreadable: Open ports: the list of open ports could not be read
ports.fix: Fix: close every port except 22, 80 and 443.
ports.how:
On the server: ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80/tcp && ufw allow 443/tcp && ufw enable
Ports published by Docker skip ufw: bind them to 127.0.0.1 in the compose file instead.
Your hosting provider's firewall (for example Hetzner Cloud Firewall) can also block ports; Aquarium can't see that one.
doctor.fix: Fix: open "Show me how" for each problem and what to do.
doctor.missing: Health check: the aquarium command is not installed on this server
doctor.missingFix: Servers set up with the Aquarium installer have it. Ask whoever runs this server.
doctor.old: Health check: the server's aquarium command is too old to report here
doctor.oldFix: Update the aquarium command on the server.
doctor.oldHow: On the server, as root, in the Aquarium folder: install -m 755 -o root -g root deploy/aquarium.py /usr/local/sbin/aquarium
doctor.timeout: Health check: took too long and was stopped
doctor.timeoutFix: Run aquarium doctor on the server to see the full result.
doctor.untrusted: Health check: skipped, because the aquarium command on the server is not protected
doctor.untrustedFix: It must be owned by root and not writable by anyone else.
tools_user.ok: The assistant's commands run as their own user ({user})
tools_user.off: The assistant's commands run as the main Aquarium user, which can read its passwords and keys
tools_user.fix: Fix: turn on the separate user for the assistant's commands.
tools_user.how:
On the server, as root, in the Aquarium folder: bash deploy/hermes-tools-setup --hermes-home <HERMES_HOME> --hermes-bin <Aquarium folder>/.venv/bin/hermes --enable
It saves a backup first and prints the rollback command. Then restart Aquarium.
two_factor.unavailable: Two-factor login for the owner: not available in this version yet
two_factor.ok: The owner signs in with two-factor login
two_factor.off: The owner has not turned on two-factor login
two_factor.fix: Fix: turn it on in step 1 (Owner account and two-factor login).
two_factor.unknown: Two-factor login: could not be checked
settingsNote: Read-only checks of this server: HTTPS, SSH sign-in, updates, open ports and the health check.
